messages:
incidents-bot: [PAGE] Sev2 - Elevated 5xx on /v1/generate from canary pool A (5m > 3%). Pager: @Ryan. Paging details: https://monitoring.redwood/alerts/ALRT-17687 :rotating_light:
Ryan: on it. pulling up canary dashboards and recent deploys. :eyes:
Ryan: quick look — spike started ~3m after deploy-bot rolled sha abcd1234 to canary-A. 5xxs are mostly 5xx-server-error and some OOMs in runtime logs.
Anna: I saw the log dup earlier, looks like KV-cache deserialization errors + `batch_flush` timing mismatch in the new batching change. Reproduces locally with long context.
Julia: confirming metric: p50 latency ok, p95 up from 320ms -> 780ms, 5xx rate to 4.8% in canary-A. Not yet in canary-B.
Ryan: can we switch traffic off the new runtime quickly? prefer not full rollback if we can circuit-break.
Devin: we have a feature-gate for the runtime: `feature_gates.runtime_v2_canary`. We can flip to route traffic back to baseline.
Ryan: do it. I'll run the command.
Ryan: ```
# disable canary runtime for prod
redwoodctl feature-gate set runtime_v2_canary false --env=prod --scope=canary-A
```
deploy-bot: feature_gate_update acknowledged. runtime_v2_canary -> false for canary-A. [action id: ag-2026-09-15-17687] :gear:
deploy-bot: traffic shift initiated: 100% -> baseline in canary-A (target 30s).
Julia: seeing 5xx drop in the next minute. 5xx from 4.8% -> 0.9% in canary-A. Good mitigation. :thumbsup:
Tereza: thanks. quick customer impact check — which customers hit the failing path?
Anna: preliminary list from logs (sampled): AcmeAnalytics, GammaRetail, and a few internal test accounts. Estimated affected requests ~1% of total live traffic; some large-context batching workloads most affected.
Ryan: good. Notifying SRE on-call for affected customers. @Tereza can you draft customer note afterwards?
Tereza: yes, will draft. keep me posted on root cause and ETA to full fix.
Anna: root cause summary: a small change in commit `abcd1234` altered batch flush ordering for quantized kernels. Under long sequences the KV cache deserializer races with a flush, sometimes leading to buffer overread -> OOM -> 5xx. Reverting that single change fixes repro locally.
Devin: I'll prepare a single-commit patch that reverts the specific reorder. Plan: revert commit locally -> run unit/integration -> canary-deploy patch to canary-A (since we've just routed baseline there, we should first re-enable canary to test) -> promote.
Devin: proposed commands:
```
# create revert branch
git checkout -b revert/batch-flush-order
git revert --no-edit abcd1234
bazel test //runtime/... //tests/integration:long_context
# build and push
ci build --sha revert-abcd1234
ci deploy --target canary-A --sha revert-abcd1234
```
Ryan: timeline?
Devin: I can have a patch build and canary deploy in ~18-22 minutes.
Julia: until patch validated keep runtime_v2_canary disabled for all canaries. We should also add a short-lived circuit breaker at the API layer for long-context requests to limit blast radius.
Ryan: I'll add a WAF rule to reject >16k token requests with 429 for 30m.
Ryan: ```
# temp rate/size guard
redwoodctl waf set-rule deny_long_contexts --max-tokens 16000 --action 429 --ttl 30m
```
deploy-bot: WAF rule applied in prod (rule-id: waf-9982).
Devin: build succeeded locally and tests pass (long_context integration passed). Kicking CI.
deploy-bot: CI build complete. Starting canary deploy for revert-abcd1234 to canary-A. canary deploy id: cd-7766.
Ryan: switching canary-A back to canary runtime to exercise patch.
Ryan: ```
redwoodctl feature-gate set runtime_v2_canary true --env=prod --scope=canary-A
```
deploy-bot: feature_gate_update acknowledged. runtime_v2_canary -> true for canary-A.
Julia: observing canary metrics now. p95 stable, 5xx at 0.2% in canary-A after patch. No OOMs in runtime logs for last 10m. :sparkles:
Tereza: customer note draft: "We temporarily routed traffic away from a new runtime due to elevated errors. We deployed a targeted revert patch and restored normal routing. A small set of high-context requests may have seen errors between X and Y. We're following up with postmortem." Will share in #customer-comm after ops review.
Ryan: I'll start handoff — I need to step into a call. Julia — taking on oncall until 12:30 UTC. Key actions taken: circuit swap -> WAF guard -> single-commit revert -> canary validated.
Julia: taking handoff, noted. I'll keep monitoring for 45m and coordinate promotion.
Anna: recommend promoting patch to remaining canary pools then prod once two hours stable. Also remove WAF guard after promotion.
Devin: scheduling promotion to canary-B in 40m.
deploy-bot: Incident update: mitigation in place, traffic stable. Remaining action: promote revert to all canaries and schedule full rollout.
incidents-bot: Incident status changed: Mitigated -> Monitoring. Next update in 30m or on status change.
Ryan: thanks team. cc @Tereza will finalize customer comms and postmortem outline. :white_check_mark:
